Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Exact utterer: Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi criticizes those who certify awakening at the mere instant of an eyebrow raise or blink.

Senses.Explanation: Raising the eyebrows and blinking is an observable facial response whose value changes with the encounter; the action itself does not certify what it means. Mazu Daoyi explicitly makes the gesture right at some times and wrong at others. A questioner says it is not yet an adept’s working, while Zhongji Kezun and Dongshan Shouchu compare formulaic gesture to confinement or a kitchen rag. A visiting monk reports it as evidence of pervasive awareness; Tianran Hanshi analyzes Mazu’s alternating use, and Chushi Fanqi condemns instant certification based on the gesture alone.

Senses.Explanation: To pronounce a case settled on the evidence or confession already supplied. Masters use the courtroom formula when delivering a decisive appraisal of a story, speaker, or ritual occasion. Baiyu Jingsi says that Śākyamuni and Ānanda are both disreputable and closes their case from the facts. Miaoyun Zhenxiong says his preceding words have already closed the case before requesting a further memorial phrase. Baichi Xingyuan quotes his teacher accepting an unnamed monk’s auspicious response as enough to close the case. Sanshan Denglai describes exposing the buddha-seat’s stolen goods and then closing the case. Shending Yikui says Xuansha’s appraisal closed the case but left an injustice still requiring redress.
